content: The SZT2 (Seizure threshold 2) homolog is a protein in humans encoded by the SZT2 gene. The protein encoded by the SZT2 gene is primarily expressed in the brain, with predominant localization in the parietal and frontal cortex, as well as in the dorsal root ganglia. It is localized to the peroxisome and is implicated in resistance to oxidative stress. Its function is thought to involve the enhancement of superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, although the protein itself does not possess direct SOD activity. Studies conducted in mice indicate that the SZT2 gene is associated with a low seizure threshold and may also play a role in promoting epileptogenesis. Mutations in the SZT2 gene have been identified as a cause of infantile encephalopathy characterized by epilepsy and dysmorphic features of the corpus callosum.
